fixed_triple.variable_convention: For v!=z, x_v=1 iff v is assigned to R; x_v=0 iff v is assigned to L.

implication_graph.name: D_{z,c,f}
construction: For each unordered edge uv in E(G-z), if cu is absent OR fv is absent, add implication arc v->u. This is the clause (x_u OR NOT x_v), forbidding u in L, v in R.
For the same edge uv, if fu is absent OR cv is absent, add implication arc u->v. This is the clause (NOT x_u OR x_v), forbidding u in R, v in L.
implication_graph.equivalent_ordered_edge_form: For every ordered adjacent pair (u,v) in G-z, if cu is absent OR fv is absent, add arc v->u.
implication_graph.clause_class: Every non-unit clause is a mixed-sign implication/order clause. No generic 2-SAT SCC satisfiability test is required.

main_equivalence.theorem: The fixed triple (z,c,f) admits an exact-channel decomposition iff Reach_D(R0) intersect L0 is empty.
necessity: Every vertex of R0 must be assigned R.
Every implication arc p->q means x_p=1 forces x_q=1.
Therefore every vertex reachable from R0 must be R in every feasible solution.
If such a reachable vertex lies in L0, it is simultaneously forced R and forced L, contradiction.
sufficiency: If R_min is disjoint from L0, assign every vertex of R_min to R and every other vertex except z to L.
R_min is successor-closed under every implication arc by construction.
Hence every mixed-sign clause is satisfied.
All forced-R units hold because R0 subseteq R_min, and all forced-L units hold because R_min is disjoint from L0.
By the previously proved 2-SAT/exact-channel equivalence, this assignment yields an exact-channel decomposition.

minimal_R.property: R_min is contained in every feasible R-side.

maximal_R.property: Every feasible R-side is contained in R_max.
maximal_R.proof: Any vertex that can reach L0 cannot be R in a feasible implication-closed assignment, otherwise implications force a vertex of L0 to R.

canonical_extremal_solutions.feasibility_relation: For every feasible fixed triple, R_min subseteq R_max.

full_solution_lattice.exact_characterization: A set R subseteq V(G)\{z} is a feasible R-side iff R0 subseteq R, R intersect L0 is empty, and R is successor-closed under D. Equivalently: R_min subseteq R subseteq R_max and R is successor-closed.
full_solution_lattice.warning: Merely lying between R_min and R_max is not sufficient; implication closure is also required.
full_solution_lattice.preorder: Define u <=_D v iff v is reachable from u in D. Feasible R-sides are exactly the upper sets of this reachability preorder satisfying the forced bounds.
full_solution_lattice.SCC_quotient: After contracting strongly connected components of D, feasible solutions are upper sets of the condensation DAG between the forced closure and forbidden predecessor region.
full_solution_lattice.lattice: The feasible R-sides form a distributive lattice under set intersection and union.

NO_DECOMPOSITION.logic: r0 is forced R; implications propagate R along the path; ell0 is therefore forced R but also forced L.
NO_DECOMPOSITION.verifier: Linear in the path length plus adjacency checks.

cf_nonedge.reason: c is forced L and f forced R; if cf were an edge, it would be a crossing edge incident with anchors, contradicting c notin P_L and f notin P_R. Equivalently, unit forces collide through the crossing constraints.

no_common_forced_neighbor.reason: Any such vertex belongs to both L0 and R0 and immediately falsifies the reachability criterion.

necessary_prefilters.role: Optional O(1)/set-intersection prefilters; they are not needed for correctness.

fixed_triple: Feasible iff the closure is disjoint from L0.
If feasible, output canonical minimal-R decomposition R_min and reconstruct ports canonically.
If infeasible, output a predecessor tree path from some r0 in R0 to the first reached ell0 in L0.
global: Enumerate eligible ordered triples (z,c,f) with c,f distinct neighbors of z.
Apply the cheap cf/common-neighbor prefilters if desired.
discovery_algorithm.total_complexity: O(m*Delta*(n+m)); hence O(n*m*(n+m)) as a coarser bound.

R_max is a valid feasible solution whenever feasible
